questions.question: Why are generics used?

options.text: Generics make code more optimised and readable
Generics add stability to your code by making more of your bugs detectable at compile time
Generics add stability to your code by making more of your bugs detectable at run time

questions.explanation: Generics add stability to your code by making more of your bugs detectable at compile time.

questions.question: Which of these type parameters is used for generic methods to return and accept any type of object?
questions.explanation: T is used for type, A type variable can be any non-primitive type you specify: any class type, any interface type, any array type, or even another type variable.

questions.question: Which of these is an correct way of defining generic method?
questions.explanation: A generic method declares type parameters in angle brackets after the method name, for example public T name<T>(T arg). C# does not put the type-parameter list before the return type (that is Java).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Generic<int> only accepts int. g.push("Csharp") is a compile-time type error; generics do not wait until run time to reject the string.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
questions.explanation: Generic<string> only accepts string. g.push(30) does not compile because int is not string.

questions.question: What does the following C# code block define?

options.text: Both Generics class declaration & Declaration of variable

questions.explanation: class Gen<T> This defines the generics declaration where 'T' is the name of type parameter. This parameter is used as a placeholder for the actual type that will be specified when a Gen object is created. Gen is a generic class. T is used to declare a variable called 'ob'.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code snippet?
Select the type argument of open constructed type?
questions.explanation: A generic type such as Gen<T> is an open constructed type because the type argument is still the parameter T. Gen<int> is closed. Gen<> is the unbound generic type used with typeof, not an open constructed type.

questions.question: Choose the correct way to call method x() of the sample class?
questions.explanation: The class is a and the method is x. Create a delegate whose signature matches x, bind it with new del(s.x) (no ref), then invoke it. ref is not used when constructing a delegate from a method group.
